newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS/HEAT BRAWL MAY RESULT IN SUSPENSIONS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS/HEAT BRAWL MAY RESULT IN SUSPENSIONS.

text.p: The NBA is expected to hand out fines and possible suspensions in the aftermath of Wednesday night's brawl between the New York Knicks and Miami Heat in Game Five of their Eastern Conference playoff series.
The game in Miami, in which the Heat staved off elimination with a 96-81 win, was marred by four ejections and an ugly melee in the final two minutes.

The brawl started after Miami forward P.J. Brown flipped Knicks guard Charlie Ward head over heels across the baseline after Ward leaned low against his legs in an effort to win position for a rebound on a free throw.

"I don't like to make a scene, but when you play dirty -- and they're a dirty bunch of guys -- I told Charlie, If you want to play football, go back to Florida State,'" Brown said about Ward, a Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback in college.
"I'm very worried about being suspended for the next game. Hopefully, (NBA vice president of operations) Rod Thorn will look at the film and he'll see that the man was trying to go for my knees."
Said Ward, "P.J. picked me up and flipped me over," said Ward. "I'm not out there to try to hurt anyone. I just tried to defend myself. The situation just got out of control."
John Wallace of the Knicks then grabbed Brown from behind and several players from the Knicks bench streamed onto the court.
The Knicks lead the best-of-seven series 3-2 with Game Six in New York on Friday.

Referee Dick Bavetta said all but two Knick players came off the bench during the skirmish, while none of the Heat players joined the fray. Leaving the bench to join in an altercation can bring fines and suspension from the league.
Thorn is expected to make a ruling on Thursday.

Brown, Ward and John Starks, who made an obscene gesture to the crowd on his way off the court, were ejected following the brawl. Shortly before the brawl, New York forward Charles Oakley was ejected for shoving Heat centre Alonzo Mourning.
The winner of the Miami-New York series will play the defending champion Chicago Bulls in the Eastern Conference finals.
